documents.text:
**HISTORIC MIX-UP: 1945 FILM "OBJECTIVE, BURMA!" MISTAKENLY NOMINATED FOR PRESTIGIOUS VIDEO GAME AWARD**

In a bizarre incident that has left the gaming and film communities stunned, the 1945 war film "Objective, Burma!" was mistakenly nominated for The Game Awards' prestigious "Best Ongoing" category. The Raoul Walsh-directed film, starring Errol Flynn, tells the story of a group of Allied soldiers on a mission to destroy a Japanese radar station in Burma during World War II. Released over 75 years ago, the film has been a classic of the war genre, but its connection to the world of video games is nonexistent. "I was shocked when I saw the nomination list," said Geoff Keighley, creator of The Game Awards. "I mean, 'Objective, Burma!' is a great film, but it's not exactly a video game. We're still trying to figure out how this happened." The mistake was reportedly made by a new intern at the awards organization, who confused the film with a fictional video game of the same name. "It was an honest mistake," said the intern, who wished to remain anonymous. "I'm a huge fan of old movies, and I must have gotten my wires crossed." The nomination has sparked a heated debate among gamers and film enthusiasts, with many taking to social media to express their confusion and amusement. "I mean, I love Errol Flynn as much as the next guy, but what's he doing in a video game award category?" tweeted @GamingGuru22. Others have seen the humor in the situation, with @FilmFan42 joking, "Maybe they're trying to start a new trend – retro film-game crossovers?" Despite the mix-up, the film's nomination has brought attention to the often-overlooked classic. "It's been a great opportunity for us to introduce the film to a new generation," said a spokesperson for the film's distributor. "Who knows, maybe we'll even see a video game adaptation of 'Objective, Burma!' in the future." The Game Awards have announced that they will be revoking the nomination and replacing it with a new contender. The ceremony is set to take place on December 10, and fans are eagerly awaiting the announcement of the corrected nominees. In the meantime, the film community is reveling in the unexpected attention, and gamers are enjoying the absurdity of it all.
